narrative.overview: This is a light desktop operating system for reading a market month without turning the work into a dashboard spectacle. White working space, soft zinc surfaces, charcoal actions, a restrained teal selection, and visible rules let the figures, evidence, and Turkish labels do the work. The sidebar keeps the working context close while the content area stays broad, dense, and calm. Colour carries state sparingly: teal locates the current path, green and red support signed values, and amber keeps incomplete evidence visible. The system is intentionally light-only and uses native controls where they already serve the workflow.
keyCharacteristics: Light zinc shell with charcoal primary actions and restrained teal selection.
Segoe UI hierarchy, tabular figures, visible rules, and compact operational density.
Native tables, selects, disclosures, and SVG trend chart retained beside three shared controls.
Explicit warning, unavailable, synthetic, and report-evidence states.

rules.name: The Accent Is Location Rule
rules.body: Teal marks focus, selection, and progress. It does not certify profit or a favourable financial result.

rules.name: The Comparable Figures Rule
rules.body: Amounts, totals, and tables use tabular numerals; numeric table columns align right and retain their units and signs.

rules.name: The Overlap-Only Depth Rule
rules.body: Shadows explain an overlay. Standard cards, rows, and figures stay flat.

rules.name: The One Glaze Per Job Rule
rules.body: Each tile has exactly one glaze, and the glaze identifies the job. Ink is used for the active-data and about tiles; cobalt, turquoise, coral, and saffron are used only for import, live connection, backup, and display.

rules.name: The Ink-Only Controls Rule
rules.body: Pressable controls inside the panel are deep ink: filled, outlined, or underlined. Glaze colours never fill or outline a button, switch, or choice.

rules.name: The Amber Is Stale Rule
rules.body: Stale and failed state replaces the band's status pill and seal with amber and always arrives with a written line. Coral identifies the backup tile and the coverage gap; it never signals failure on its own.

rules.name: The Counted Days Rule
rules.body: The coverage lead is the only large figure on the page. It counts days, not money, and it stays tabular.

rules.name: The Aligned Courses Rule
rules.body: Tiles in one course share subgrid rows. A longer band line pushes down every body in that course, never just its own.

rules.name: The Glaze Is The Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth belongs to the band's glaze sheen. Tiles never take a drop shadow.

scopedWorlds.appliesTo: The Ayarlar settings page and the sidebar-footer live badge.
scopedWorlds.overview: Ayarlar is an approved second visual world, deliberately not consistent with the ledger. It is a panel of glaze-white çini tiles set in warm grout. Each tile is one job: a saturated glaze band names it, a round eight-point seal carries its condition, and its body holds only the facts and the next action. Colour is louder here than in the ledger, but it stays on the bands and seals; every pressable control in the panel is deep ink. The world is scoped. Its tokens carry the `settings-` prefix and apply inside the settings page, plus the live badge in the sidebar footer. The Quiet Market Ledger remains the system for other surfaces except the selected Özet control desk.
keyCharacteristics: Glaze tiles separated by a 6px warm-grout gap on a grout page ground.
Five glaze bands (ink, cobalt, turquoise, coral, saffron), one per job, with a seal and an optional status pill.
Deep ink as the only colour on pressable controls; primary, outline, and quiet underlined variants.
A coverage strip drawn to exact date proportion up to today, with a hatched coral gap.
Segoe UI and tabular figures, inherited from the ledger.
dos: Do give each settings job its own tile, glaze, seal, one plain band line, and only its next action.
Do keep every pressable control deep ink: primary fill, 1.5px outline, or quiet underline.
Do pair every stale, failed, or unknown seal with written state in the status pill or a note.
Do draw the coverage strip to true date proportion up to today and state the gap in days.
Do align tiles within a course on shared subgrid rows and keep the 6px grout gap at every width.
donts: Don't fill or outline a button, switch, or choice with cobalt, turquoise, coral, or saffron.
Don't carry glaze tokens, the grout ground, or tile bands onto ledger workspaces; only the sidebar live badge leaves the settings page.
Don't give tiles a drop shadow; the grout gap and the band's glaze carry the depth.
Don't imply financial meaning for source rows on a tile or the coverage strip; source coverage stays labelled as record counts.

dos: Do keep the period, cutoff, synthetic identity, and evidence state readable where the owner works.
Do use the light paper-and-zinc surfaces, visible separators, and tabular figures to support scanning.
Do use teal for the current path and keyboard focus, and pair positive, negative, and amber colour with written context.
Do preserve native table scrolling and disclosure behavior when extending an existing workflow.
donts: Don't restore the superseded navy rail or dark component variants. Cobalt actions are authorized within the selected Özet surface.
Don't use teal, green, or red alone to assert financial meaning.
Don't replace missing evidence with a zero or hide it to make a compact view cleaner.
Don't add a generated control framework where the native table, select, disclosure, or chart already owns the task.
